sentence-level. A sentence is kept when it contains one of: is/are/was/were/can/could/will/would/shall/may/might/do/does/did/has/have + not + (supported|available|released|possible|permitted|allowed|covered|provided|delivered|offered); does/do not support; is/are unsupported; not supported by/for/in/with/on; no plans/support to/for; out of scope; is not part of; is/are excluded from; is/are not in scope.

dropped 90 sentences opening with a conditional connector (If/When/Unless/Since/Because/While/Although/In case/...) and 20 whose negated subject is itself a conditional clause, because those state a condition rather than a product limitation; dropped 4 affirmative sentences ("You can ...") whose negation sits in a parenthetical relative clause; dropped 1 describing a transient example state; dropped 5 whose subject could not be isolated.
capability=the title of the SAP topic the sentence was read from, verbatim. It is SAP's heading, NOT an aptus classification.

scope_item_ids=scope item codes appearing IN THE SENTENCE ITSELF and present in the 2608 scope item set (sap-references/2608 Scope sheet, plus the codes in the published Available Interfaces table). Empty on most rows because SAP writes these statements about features, not scope items — an empty cell is not a claim that no scope item is affected.

country=the country/region deliverable the topic belongs to; where the topic is not in a country deliverable, a country named explicitly in the sentence. Empty means the statement is product-wide or SAP did not name a country.

what_is_not_supported=mechanically extracted from SAP's own sentence: the text preceding the negation verb, after the last connector (however/but/although/while/;/because/since/therefore) and with a leading conjunction stripped. Where nothing precedes the negation, the text following it is used. No wording was added.
sap_statement_verbatim=the sentence exactly as SAP published it, whitespace-normalised only. Never softened, never paraphrased, never turned into a caveat.

source_type=Help on every row. SAP Notes and Knowledge Base Articles live behind authentication on me.sap.com and were NOT read in this pass, so the KBA and Note families named in the brief are still unharvested — this file is the Help-portal slice of the register, not the register.
source_id=the SAP loio, SAP's own stable document id for the topic
released_on=empty on every row: help.sap.com publishes a content release (2608) for the document, not a release date for the individual statement. The release for every row in this file is 2608.

future_support_stated=a clause from the same or the next sentence in which SAP says something about future support (no plans / not planned / in a future release / currently not / as of now / not yet), verbatim. Empty means SAP said nothing about the future there, NOT that support is planned.
